look_here_first: LOOK FIRST underground: tough/wiry stolons and usually small (~3–8 mm) tubers distinguish purple nutsedge in combination with persistent, often purplish/red-brown ~2.6–3.4 mm scales. Don't rely on reddish seedhead color by itself.

project_inclusion.range_basis: POWO lists Cyperus rotundus as introduced in Texas; retain in learner for weed lookalike recognition only, exclude from native-only calculations.

morphology_keys.habit: Introduced perennial sedge, frequently colonial in cultivated or disturbed ground.
morphology_keys.underground: Hard, wiry stolons bearing tubers commonly 3–8 mm; compare with yellow nutsedge softer stolons and usually larger tubers.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Terminal umbel-like rays with flattened spikelets; scales often red-purple-brown but variable.
morphology_keys.scales: Persistent mature floral scales often ~2.6–3.4 mm with reddish/purple tint; ranges overlap other taxa.
morphology_keys.fruit: One-seeded achene; macro of scale and fruit needed for strong ID.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Yellow nutsedge's softer/spongy stolons and often smaller/yellower floral scales are better differentiators than inflorescence color. Do not identify either without multiple characters.
comparisons.cautions: Photo source geography is not evidence of three-county target zone native range; colors and many measurements overlap, require mature specimens.
